descriptionChirho: A spoken or written word, message, or divine utterance (Arabic kalima/kalam, Korean malsseum/mal, Swahili neno), including all possessive and prepositional inflections referring to speech content.
A matter, affair, or issue of practical concern requiring attention or action (Arabic amr, Korean il, Swahili jambo), including legal cases, disputes, and situational affairs.
An indefinite thing or entity, often in negative constructions meaning nothing or in questions meaning anything (Arabic shay', Korean geot, Swahili kitu).
Recorded deeds, historical acts, or annals of a person or nation, as in the formulaic 'the acts/chronicles of king X' (Arabic umur/akhbar, Korean haengjeok/yeondaegi, Swahili mambo ya).
Events or things that happened, often in plural as 'these things' referring to a sequence of occurrences (Arabic al-umur, Korean geu ildeul, Swahili mambo haya).
Used in comparative constructions meaning 'like the thing' or 'according to the manner of', referring to the way or fashion of something (Arabic kal-amr, Korean il-gachi, Swahili kama jambo).
The reason or cause for something, used in constructions meaning 'on account of' or 'for the sake of' (Arabic sabab/amr, Korean il-ui, Swahili sababu).
